title: The Thank-You Address Lives in Account Settings, Not the Plan

intelligence.essence: **THE THANK-YOU ADDRESS IS ACCOUNT-LEVEL (~19:44Z, his question):** the plan has only two Update buttons (Plan info, Pricing) — there is no thank-you spot inside any plan, because Auto Return is an account setting, not a plan setting. It lives in PayPal Settings → Account settings → Website payments → Website Preferences → Auto Return (On) + Return URL — one setting for the whole account, covering all nine plans at once. **WAIT until the link is live before setting it** — if someone paid before the link exists they would land on the wrong page. **HOW IT GETS TRACKED:** the buyer finishes paying, PayPal sends them back to the thank-you Smart Link, the link counts the return (who, which plan, when), then passes them on to the thank-you page; the Dashboard shows it as "returned from PayPal." **MAX YEARLY VERIFIED BY HIS EYE (~19:50Z, his screenshots):** plan P-7Y535865SR1836345NLXDQ6I, Status On — setup $0.00 CAD · trial $0.00 CAD, every 9 days, 1 cycle · subscription $600.00 CAD, every 1 year. The 9-day trial is CONFIRMED live on the plan. Yearly = half ($600 vs $1,200) holds. Prices charge in CAD. **NOTE:** the Return URL as answered was https://nayanet.app/thank-you — superseded ~19:55Z by his dash rule, SN-2347: the slug is `thankyou`, Return URL https://nayanet.app/thankyou.
intelligence.human_view: He did the right thing — he went looking for where the thank-you page goes, opened the plan, and found nowhere to put it. Only two Update buttons. No thank-you spot. And the reason is not that something is missing from the plan: the thank-you address never belonged in the plan. It belongs one level up, in the account — Settings, Account settings, Website payments, Website Preferences — Auto Return, turned On, with the Return URL. One setting, the whole account, all nine plans at once. That is why there is no spot in the plan to find, and why looking harder in the plan would never have found it. And the tracking follows from the same shape: PayPal sends the buyer back to the thank-you Smart Link, the link counts the return — who, which plan, when — and passes them on to the page, and the Dashboard reads "returned from PayPal." The screenshots also settled the plan itself: Max Yearly, $600 for the year, $0 setup, the 9-day trial right there on it. The trial is real, and it is live on the plan. One caution, given in the same breath as the answer: do not set the Return URL until the link is live — a buyer who pays before the link exists lands on the wrong page, and a wrong landing is worse than a wait.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine you buy something in a shop and the shop has to send you back to a special "thank you" door when you finish paying. You look for that door inside the little box that says "Max Yearly" — but it's not in the box. It's in the big settings room for the whole shop, one switch that works for every box at once. You flip it on, you write down the address of the thank-you door, and from then on everyone who pays walks through that door — and we count every single person who walks through, so we know who paid and for what. And the plan itself is right: $600 for the whole year, nothing to set up, nine days free to try first.

It lives one floor up, in the account settings, where one switch covers everything: you turn Auto Return on, you write in the return address, and every plan — all nine of them — uses the same one. That's why the plan has no spot for it, and that's how the counting works: when someone finishes paying, PayPal walks them back through our thank-you link, we count them, and then they see the thank-you page. And his screenshots showed the plan itself is exactly right — Max Yearly, $600 for the year, nothing to set up, nine days free. intelligence.what_it_means:
1. **No thank-you spot exists inside any plan** — the plan has only two Update buttons (Plan info, Pricing), and that is by PayPal's design, not a gap.
2. **Auto Return is account-level:** Settings → Account settings → Website payments → Website Preferences → Auto Return (On) + Return URL.
3. **One setting covers all nine plans at once.**
4. **Wait until the link is live before setting it** — a buyer who pays first lands on the wrong page.
5. **How it gets tracked:** PayPal → thank-you Smart Link (counts the return: who, which plan, when) → thank-you page; Dashboard shows "returned from PayPal."
6. **Max Yearly verified live by his eye:** P-7Y535865SR1836345NLXDQ6I, $0 setup, $0 trial every 9 days × 1 cycle, $600 CAD every 1 year; yearly = half ($600 vs $1,200); prices in CAD.
7. **The Return URL given in the answer (nayanet.app/thank-you) was superseded ~19:55Z by the dash rule (SN-2347): the slug is `thankyou`.**
